subject: Potential Computational Speed up in INLA and inlabru

messages.author: d7ee34c7589817da
messages.subject: Potential Computational Speed up in INLA and inlabru
parts:
Dear inla team,

I am currently running a model that uses INLA within MCMC. The INLA model I am fitting is a simple spatial Poisson regression with the log rate driven by a Gaussian process on a regular grid. 

Even though the computational time of INLA is pretty fast (with 8 cores, it takes roughly 1.8 seconds), putting it into a MCMC setting is still quite computationally costly: obtaining 10000 MCMC sample would require roughly 5 hours.

Are there any ways to further reduce the computational cost for INLA in this case?

Specifically, the only thing that I need from the Poisson regression model is the log-marginal likelihood and the posterior mode of the linear predictor (log-rate) at the spatial grid. 

So I am wondering if there are inla options that I can set so that INLA only needs to compute the previously mentioned quantities to save time?

Thank you very much!

Best,
David

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Potential Computational Speed up in INLA and inlabru
parts:
you can try something like this. takes from from 12s to 8s in the example below.



Germany = cbind(Germany,region.struct=Germany$region)

formula3 = Y ~ f(region.struct,model="besag",graph=g, constr = T) +
f(region,model="iid") + f(x, model="rw2")

tref <- Sys.time()
for(i in 1:10) {
r = inla(formula3,
family="poisson",
data=Germany,
E=E,
verbose = !TRUE,
num.threads = "1:1")
}
print(Sys.time() - tref)

tref <- Sys.time()
r.prev <- NULL
for(i in 1:10) {
r = inla(formula3,
family="poisson",
data=Germany,
E=E,
verbose = !TRUE,
num.threads = "1:1",
control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb",
control.vb = list(enable = FALSE)),
control.compute = list(return.marginals = FALSE),
control.mode = list(result = r.prev, restart = TRUE))
r.prev <- r
}
print(Sys.time() - tref)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Potential Computational Speed up in INLA and inlabru
parts:
Hi David,

In addition to what Havard has mentioned, you can try importance sampling with INLA (see links below). This will have a better performance as it can be parallelized effectively and it can take your computations from hours to a few minutes. The code for the examples in the papers below is available from GitHub as well.

Best,

Virgilio

https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10618600.2022.2067551

https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11222-022-10122-1

Part of this time is how its written: R write files with data/model, then the
inlaprogram starts up in a separate process, read files, build model, do things,
write the results to files. then R read the results from the file, prepare the
R-object and cleanup. Not an ideal situation for use within mcmc.

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Potential Computational Speed up in INLA and inlabru
parts:
Hi,

Also, I have always regarded the INLA within MCMC paper as a “proof of concept” to show that INLA can also be used as a “device" to reduce the dimension of your model (by means of computing the marginal likelihood conditional on some hyper parameters) and to fit models that are not latent GMRF models. I think the this is a great feature of INLA that it is often neglected. In practice, I would use importance sampling (as mentioned in my previous e-mail), numerical integration [1,2] or a grid/CCD strategy [3].

Best,

Virgilio

[1] https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2211675314000037?via%3Dihub

[2] https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v063i20

[3] https://academic.oup.com/jrsssc/article/68/1/199/7058418
